title_orig: Ἐκκλησιαστικὴ ἱστορία I.7 (quoting Julius Africanus, Letter to Aristides)
title_es: Historia eclesiástica I.7 (cita de la carta de Julio Africano a Aristides)
title_en: Church History I.7 (quoting Julius Africanus, Letter to Aristides)
author: Eusebius of Caesarea, quoting Julius Africanus
date: Eusebius c. 324 AD; Africanus 3rd century (approx.; date not on the page)
genre: Church history; quoted Christian letter on the gospel genealogies
edition_original: Eusebius, Historia ecclesiastica (Greek text not located; not read)
edition_english: Church History, Book I, trans. Arthur Cushman McGiffert, NPNF2 vol. 1, ed. Philip Schaff and Henry Wace (1890)
licence: Page carries no licence line in the text read; the translation is NPNF2 vol. 1 (1890), public domain
notes: Africanus: Matthew's and Luke's genealogies explained by levirate marriage (law) vs natural descent; Joseph 'son of Jacob by nature, son of Eli according to law'; Mary of the same tribe (end of 1.7).

author: Eusebius of Caesarea, quoting Hegesippus
date: Eusebius c. 324 AD; Hegesippus 2nd century (approx.; not on the page)
genre: Church history; report of an earlier writer
edition_original: Eusebius, Historia ecclesiastica (Greek not located; not read)
edition_english: Church History, Book III, trans. Arthur Cushman McGiffert, NPNF2 vol. 1 (1890)
licence: Page carries no licence line in the text read; NPNF2 vol. 1 (1890), public domain
notes: Vespasian's search for David's line (3.12); Domitian and grandsons of Jude (3.19–20); Symeon son of Clopas accused as 'a descendant of David and a Christian' (3.32). Hegesippus is known only through Eusebius.

date: late 4th century AD (approx.; not on the page)

licence: Public domain translation (NPNF1 vol. 10, 1888); page licence not seen
notes: Hom. 1.14 lists the questions ('the genealogy of Joseph ... who was not father of Christ'); Hom. 2.7–8 answers via endogamy and the custom of tracing men's genealogies.
